title: Designing a URL Shortener
contentMd:
Scope first: assume 100 million new short links per month and a 100:1 read-to-write ratio, so writes land around 40 per second while reads reach roughly 4,000 per second. Storage over five years lands near 3 TB. Those numbers immediately tell you the service is read-heavy and needs a cache in front of the database from day one.

The core question is how to generate the key. Hashing the long URL with MD5 and taking the first seven Base62 characters will eventually collide, so you need a uniqueness check. A cleaner approach many candidates miss is a distributed ID generator that hands out monotonically increasing numbers, which you then encode into Base62. There is no collision risk at all, and the key stays short because Base62 packs roughly 3.7 bits into every character.

For redirects, return a 301 for permanent links so browsers cache it and your server is taken out of the loop, or a 302 when you need click analytics. Either way the hot path is the same: CDN or cache lookup, database on miss, then a header-only HTTP response. Keep it stateless so you can add nodes freely.

Finally, name the tradeoffs out loud. SQL gives you uniqueness constraints for free; NoSQL gives easier horizontal scaling but you must handle duplicates yourself. Custom aliases, expiry, and per-link analytics are the natural follow-ups interviewers love to probe.
contentCn:
先界定规模：假设每月新增一亿条短链接，读写比为 100:1，那么写入约为每秒 40 次，而读取约为每秒 4000 次。按五年计算，存储量大约在 3 TB 左右。这些数字立刻告诉你，这个服务是重读的，并且从第一天起就需要在数据库前面加一层缓存。

核心问题是如何生成这个 key。对长网址做 MD5 哈希再取 Base62 的前七个字符，最终一定会发生碰撞，因此必须做唯一性校验。很多候选人会漏掉一种更干净的做法：用一个分布式 ID 生成器发放单调递增的数字，再把它编码成 Base62。这种做法完全不存在碰撞风险，而且由于 Base62 每个字符能承载约 3.7 比特，key 依然很短。

跳转时应该使用 301 还是 302：永久链接用 301，浏览器会缓存它，你的服务器就被排除在链路之外；如果你需要点击统计，就用 302。无论哪种，热路径都是一样的：先查 CDN 或缓存，未命中再查数据库，然后返回一个只有响应头的 HTTP 报文。保持无状态，这样你可以随意扩容。

最后要把权衡说出口。关系型数据库免费给了你唯一性约束；NoSQL 更容易水平扩展，但重复数据必须你自己处理。自定义别名、过期时间以及按链接统计访问量，都是面试官喜欢继续追问的天然延伸话题。

title: Rate Limiter Algorithms Explained
contentMd:
Every rate limiter answers the same question: has this caller spent too much of its budget inside the current window? Fixed window counters are the simplest answer, one counter per key per minute, but they allow up to twice the limit at boundaries, since a burst can land at 0:59 and another immediately after at 1:00.

Sliding window logs fix that by storing a timestamp per request and counting how many fall inside the trailing window. Accurate, yes, but memory grows with traffic. Sliding window counters approximate it with memory proportional to window size, blending the current and previous bucket by the elapsed fraction, which is what most production systems actually ship.

Token bucket and leaky bucket model flow differently. A token bucket refills at a steady rate and lets bursts through up to its capacity, matching how real APIs behave. A leaky bucket drains at a constant rate and therefore smooths bursts into uniform output, which is better when protecting a downstream service that cannot absorb spikes at all.

Placement matters as much as the algorithm. Enforce limits at the gateway or the edge so rejected requests never touch your application. Store counters in Redis using atomic increment with expiry so check-and-set cannot race, and return 429 with a Retry-After header. Decide early whether keys are per-user, per-IP, or per-API-key, and whether the budget is counted per node or globally.
contentCn:
所有限流器回答的都是同一个问题：这个调用方在当前窗口里是不是已经花超了预算？固定窗口计数器是最简单的答案——每个 key 每分钟一个计数器——但它在边界处会放行高达两倍的额度，因为一次突发可能落在 0:59，另一次紧接着落在 1:00。

滑动窗口日志通过为每次请求保存一个时间戳、并统计落在过去窗口之内的数量来修复这个问题。它确实精确，但内存会随流量线性增长。滑动窗口计数器用与窗口大小成正比的内存来近似它：按已流逝的比例混合当前和上一个桶，这也是大多数生产系统真正采用的方案。

令牌桶和漏桶对流量的建模方式不同。令牌桶以恒定速率补充令牌，并允许不超过容量的突发通过，这与真实世界中 API 的行为相符。漏桶以恒定速率出水，因而把突发抹平成均匀的输出，这更适合保护完全无法吸收尖峰的下游服务。

部署位置和算法本身同样重要。在网关或边缘执行限流，被拒绝的请求就永远不会碰到你的应用。把计数器放在 Redis 里，用带过期时间的原子自增，这样「先查后写」就不会产生竞争；返回 429 并带上 Retry-After 头。还要尽早决定是按用户、按 IP 还是按 API key 计数，以及配额是按节点计还是全局计。

title: Consistent Hashing Without the Hand-Waving
contentMd:
Naive hashing maps a key to a node with hash(key) mod N. Add or remove a node and N changes, so nearly every key remaps at once. For a cache cluster that means a storm of misses hammering your origin the moment you scale.

Consistent hashing fixes this by placing both nodes and keys on the same circular hash space, typically 0 to 2^32. Each key walks clockwise to the next node it finds. When a node joins or leaves, only keys in its immediate arc move, roughly 1/N of the total.

Even that is uneven in practice, so add virtual nodes: each physical server claims a few hundred points on the ring. This spreads load statistically even, lets you weight machines by capacity, and makes removal graceful without a full reshuffle.

The same idea powers request routing, sharding, and distributed stores like Dynamo and Cassandra. Interviewers often ask how you would locate a key in O(log N): keep ring positions in a sorted structure and binary search. Remember that consistent hashing balances load but does not make it perfect; hot keys still need replication or dedicated handling.
contentCn:
朴素的哈希用 hash(key) mod N 把 key 映射到节点。一旦增删节点，N 就变了，于是几乎所有 key 同时都要重新映射。对一个缓存集群来说，这意味着你刚刚扩容的那一刻，大量未命中会像风暴一样打到源站。

一致性哈希解决了这个问题：它把节点和 key 放在同一个环形哈希空间上，通常是 0 到 2^32。每个 key 沿顺时针方向走到它遇到的下一个节点。当某个节点加入或离开时，只有它相邻弧段上的 key 会移动，大约占总量的 1/N。

即便如此，实际负载仍然不均，所以要引入虚拟节点：每台物理服务器在环上占据几百个点。这样负载在统计上是均匀的，还能按机器容量分配权重，并且让节点的移除变得优雅，无需整体重排。

同样的思想支撑着请求路由、分库分表，以及 Dynamo、Cassandra 这类分布式存储系统。面试官常问如何以 O(log N) 定位一个 key：把环上的位置放进有序结构里做二分查找。记住一致性哈希能均衡负载但并不完美；热点 key 仍然需要副本或专门的处理手段。
titleCn: 不绕弯子地理解一致性哈希

title: Designing a News Feed System
contentMd:
A news feed is fundamentally a fan-out problem. A celebrity with ten million followers posting once should not mean ten million synchronous writes, yet a user with two hundred followers gets a far better experience if their timeline is already materialized by the time they open the app.

The standard answer is a hybrid. Fan out on write for ordinary users: when someone posts, push the post ID into the timeline lists of their followers, stored in Redis as capped lists. Then switch to fan out on read for celebrities, where their followers merge that author's recent posts into their own timeline at query time. The threshold between the two is a tunable number.

The timeline itself is best stored as references rather than full post bodies, so edits and deletions propagate naturally. Keep perhaps the last 800 IDs per user and let older reads fall through to the database. When a user opens the app you make a few Redis range reads, hydrate them from a post service, then rank and return one page.

Call out the rough edges: users who follow thousands of accounts, deleted or blocked authors, and the ranking layer that turns reverse-chronological order into something personalized. Mention pagination by cursor rather than offset, so concurrent inserts do not shift results under the reader.
contentCn:
信息流本质上是一个扇出（fan-out）问题。一个拥有一千万粉丝的名人发一条内容，不应该意味着一千万次同步写入；但一个只有两百粉丝的用户，如果打开 App 时他的时间线已经预先生成好了，体验会好得多。

标准答案是混合方案。对普通用户采用写时扇出：某人发帖时，把 post ID 推送到其粉丝的时间线列表里，这些列表用 Redis 的定长列表存储。而对名人改用读时扇出——他们的粉丝在查询时才把该作者的近期帖子合并进自己的时间线。两者之间的阈值是一个可调参数。

时间线本身最好存的是引用而不是完整的帖子内容，这样编辑和删除就能自然传播。每个用户保留最近大约 800 个 ID，更早的读取则回落到数据库。用户打开 App 时，你做几次 Redis 范围读取，从帖子服务补齐内容，再排序并返回一页。

还要主动指出那些粗糙的边界：关注了成千上万个账号的用户、被删除或屏蔽的作者，以及把逆序时间排列改造成个性化排序的排序层。补充说明分页应该用游标而不是偏移量，否则并发插入会让读者眼前的结果错位。

title: Sharding Strategies and Their Consequences
contentMd:
Sharding splits one logical table across many physical databases so writes and storage scale past a single machine. The decision that dominates everything else is the shard key, because it determines whether your queries stay local or fan out to every node.

Range-based sharding assigns contiguous key ranges to shards. It keeps range scans fast but creates hotspots when traffic follows the newest data, which it usually does. Hash-based sharding applies a hash function and mods by shard count: distribution is even, but range queries must touch every shard. Directory-based sharding keeps an explicit lookup table mapping key to shard, the most flexible option, at the cost of an extra hop and another component that must never go down.

Whatever you choose, plan for growth. Rebalancing data is painful, so many teams shard by a stable attribute like tenant or user ID and accept that a few cross-shard queries will be slow. Others use consistent hashing with virtual nodes so adding capacity becomes an incremental operation.

Secondary indexes are the classic trap: an index on email does not exist globally, so you either maintain a separate global index table or scatter-gather across all shards. Say this out loud in an interview, along with how you handle distributed joins, global IDs, and resharding without downtime. The double-write and backfill pattern is usually the expected answer.
contentCn:
分库分表把一张逻辑表拆分到多台物理数据库上，使写入和存储能够突破单机上限。决定一切的是分片键，因为它决定了你的查询是本地命中，还是要扇出到每一个节点。

基于范围的分片把连续的 key 区间分配给各个分片。它让范围扫描很快，但当流量总是追着最新数据时就会产生热点，而现实通常正是如此。基于哈希的分片先做哈希再对分片数取模：分布均匀，但范围查询必须打到每个分片。基于目录的分片维护一张显式的查找表，把 key 映射到分片，它最灵活，代价是多一次跳转，以及多出一个绝不能挂掉的组件。

无论选哪种，都要为增长做打算。数据再平衡非常痛苦，所以很多团队按租户或用户 ID 这类稳定属性来分片，并接受少数跨分片查询会比较慢。另一些团队用带虚拟节点的一致性哈希，让加容量变成一个增量动作。

二级索引是经典的陷阱：建立在 email 上的索引并不全局存在，所以要么单独维护一张全局索引表，要么在所有分片上做 scatter-gather。面试时要把这些说出来，连同你如何处理分布式 join、全局 ID，以及如何不停机重新分片——双写加回填模式通常就是期待听到的答案。

title: Read Replicas and Read/Write Splitting
contentMd:
Once reads dominate, the cheapest win is to stop sending them to the primary. A read replica streams the primary's write-ahead log and replays it, so one node absorbs writes while several absorb reads. Most web workloads are ninety percent reads or more, so three replicas can nearly triple read capacity immediately.

The catch is replication lag. Binary log shipping is asynchronous by default, so a replica can fall milliseconds or seconds behind. If a user writes a comment and immediately refreshes, they may not see it, which is the read-after-write inconsistency interviewers always ask about. Practical mitigations include reading your own writes from the primary for a short window after mutation, routing by session, or checking a log sequence number before serving the read.

Routing itself needs care. Proxy it in middleware or a database proxy, but make sure ORM-level writes never leak to replicas, and handle failover so a dead replica is ejected from the pool rather than erroring every request.

Replicas buy read throughput, not write throughput, and each one is a full copy of your data. If write volume is the bottleneck, replicas will not save you; you need sharding. Replicas carrying long analytical queries also need isolation, or reporting jobs will stall them.
contentCn:
一旦读请求占了主导，最省事的优化就是别再让它们打到主库。只读副本通过流式接收主库的预写日志并重放来实现：一个节点承接写入，若干节点承接读取。多数 Web 业务的读占比在九成以上，所以加三个副本几乎能立刻让读容量接近三倍。

问题在于复制延迟。binlog 传输默认是异步的，因此副本可能落后几毫秒甚至几秒。用户刚发完评论立刻刷新，就有可能看不到自己的数据——这正是面试官必问的「读己之所写」不一致。可行的缓解办法包括：变更后一小段时间内的自身读取仍走主库、按会话路由，或者在返回数据前检查日志序列号。

路由本身也需要小心。可以在中间件或数据库代理层做，但必须确保 ORM 层的写请求永远不会泄漏到副本上，并且要处理故障转移，让挂掉的副本被移出连接池，而不是让每个请求都报错。

副本买来的是读吞吐，不是写吞吐，而且每个副本都是数据的一份完整拷贝。如果瓶颈在写入量上，副本救不了你，你得做分片。承载长耗时分析查询的副本还需要隔离，否则会被报表任务拖住。

title: CDN and Edge Caching in Practice
contentMd:
A content delivery network moves your bytes closer to users by caching them at hundreds of edge locations. A request from Lisbon is answered in Lisbon instead of crossing an ocean, which cuts latency from hundreds of milliseconds to tens and keeps that traffic away from your origin entirely.

Static assets are the easy case: images, JavaScript bundles, and video segments get a long max-age plus a content hash in the filename, so you can cache forever and invalidate simply by changing the URL. HTML is harder because it must stay fresh; use short TTLs with stale-while-revalidate so users never wait for a revalidation round trip.

The interesting design questions start at the cache key and invalidation. The key must include everything that changes the response: host, path, selected query parameters, and often cookies or a device hint. Purge by surrogate key rather than by URL, so one API call drops every page containing a given product. If purge APIs are too slow, lean on versioned URLs instead.

CDNs also terminate TLS, absorb DDoS traffic, run edge functions for personalization, and act as your first WAF. In an interview, distinguish pull-based origins where the CDN fetches on miss from push-based origins where you upload proactively, and admit honestly what should never be cached: per-user HTML, payment responses, and anything behind authorization.
contentCn:
内容分发网络把你的数据缓存到成百上千个边缘节点，从而离用户更近。来自里斯本的请求就在里斯本被应答，不必跨越重洋，延迟从几百毫秒降到几十毫秒，而且这部分流量完全不会打到你的源站。

静态资源是最容易处理的一类：图片、JavaScript 包和视频分片设置较长的 max-age，并在文件名里带上内容哈希，这样你就可以永久缓存，只需换 URL 就能失效。HTML 更难，因为它必须保持新鲜：用较短的 TTL 配 stale-while-revalidate，让用户永远不必等待一次校验往返。

真正有意思的设计问题从缓存键和失效开始。缓存键必须包含所有会改变响应的因素：主机、路径、选定的查询参数，通常还包括 Cookie 或设备标识。清除缓存应该按代理键（surrogate key）而不是按 URL，这样一次 API 调用就能丢弃包含某个商品的所有页面。如果清除接口太慢，那就依赖带版本号的 URL。

CDN 还能终结 TLS、吸收 DDoS 流量、运行边缘函数做个性化，并充当第一道 WAF。面试时要区分两种回源方式：拉模式下 CDN 在未命中时才回源，推模式下你主动上传；同时要诚实地说出哪些内容绝不能缓存——按用户定制的 HTML、支付响应，以及所有受授权保护的内容。
titleEn: CDN and Edge Caching in Practice
titleCn: 实践中的 CDN 与边缘缓存

title: Designing a Chat System
contentMd:
Start with the shape of the traffic: chat is long-lived, stateful, and bidirectional. Polling is trivially simple but wasteful at scale, so use WebSockets for a persistent full-duplex channel, with server-sent events as a reasonable fallback when clients only need downstream pushes.

Because connections are stateful, you need a registry mapping each user ID to the server currently holding their socket. Store it in Redis rather than local memory so any gateway can find anyone. When Alice sends to Bob, the message service writes the message to storage, looks up Bob's connection server, and forwards it there; if Bob is offline the message waits in a queue and a push notification wakes him later.

Storage should be append-oriented and partitioned by conversation ID, so one chat's history is read sequentially from a single shard. Give every message a monotonically increasing sequence number within its conversation, letting clients request only what happened after their last known seq. That one detail makes reconnection, ordering, and read receipts tractable.

Group chats are where designs die. Fan out per recipient rather than once per group message once groups get large, cap group size, and treat presence data like typing indicators and online status as ephemeral values in a TTL store, never in the durable message store. Only raise end-to-end encryption if message bodies should be opaque to you.
contentCn:
先看流量的形态：聊天是长连接、有状态、双向的。轮询实现起来最简单，但在规模化后极其浪费，因此用 WebSocket 建立持久的全双工通道；如果客户端只需要下行推送，SSE 也是个合情合理的降级方案。

因为连接是有状态的，你需要一份注册表，把每个用户 ID 映射到当前持有其 socket 的服务器。把它存在 Redis 里而不是本地内存中，这样任何网关都能找到任何人。当 Alice 给 Bob 发消息时，消息服务先落库，再查出 Bob 所在的连接服务器并转发过去；如果 Bob 离线，消息就在队列里等待，稍后由推送通知把他唤醒。

存储应当面向追加，并按会话 ID 分区，这样一个聊天的历史可以从单个分片顺序读出。给每条消息分配一个会话内单调递增的序列号，客户端就只需请求其已知最大 seq 之后的内容。仅这一个设计细节，就让重连、排序和已读回执都变得可解。

群聊是设计崩塌的地方。当群变大时，按收件人做写入扇出，而不是每条群消息只扇出一次；要给群规模设上限；把正在输入、在线状态这类「在场」数据当作临时值放进带 TTL 的存储里，绝不要放进持久的消息库。只有在消息内容本应对你不可见时，才需要提端到端加密。
titleCn: 设计一个即时通讯系统

title: Designing a Notification Service
contentMd:
A notification service exists to decouple the business events that trigger messages from the delivery channels that carry them. The moment an order service knows a package shipped, it should publish an event and forget about it; everything downstream belongs to you.

So the core is an event bus plus a fan-out layer. Producers emit domain events to Kafka or a managed queue. Consumers read them, resolve each user's contact list and channel preferences, pick a template, localize it, then drop rendered messages onto per-channel queues for push, email, SMS, or in-app delivery.

Each channel worker then owns its own ugly details. Push requires maintaining device tokens and talking to APNs or FCM, including retiring invalid tokens quietly. Email needs provider reputation management and bounce handling. SMS costs money and has per-country rules, so put hard budgets and per-user throttles in front of it. Every hop should retry with exponential backoff and land failures in a dead letter queue.

Two reliability requirements define the design. First, deduplication: retries and provider callbacks deliver the same event twice, so carry an idempotency key. Second, preference honesty: respect quiet hours, per-topic opt-outs, and channel fallback, and make the pipeline observable with per-channel delivery rates, because sent, delivered, and opened are three different numbers.
contentCn:
通知服务的存在意义，是把触发消息的业务事件与真正发送消息的投递渠道解耦。订单服务一旦知道包裹已发货，就应该发布一个事件然后撒手不管；下游的一切都属于你。

所以它的核心是事件总线加扇出层。生产者把领域事件发到 Kafka 或托管队列；消费者读取事件，解析每个用户的联系方式和渠道偏好，挑选模板、做本地化，再把渲染后的消息投递到推送、邮件、短信或站内信各自的渠道队列中。

随后每个渠道的 worker 各自处理一堆脏活。推送要维护设备令牌并和 APNs 或 FCM 通信，还要悄悄淘汰失效令牌。邮件需要管理服务商信誉并处理退信。短信要花钱，且各国规则不同，所以必须在前面加上硬性预算和按用户限流。每一跳都要用指数退避重试，并把失败的消息落进死信队列。

有两个可靠性需求定义了整个设计。其一是去重：重试和服务商回调会把同一个事件送两次，所以必须携带幂等键。其二是尊重用户偏好：遵守免打扰时段、按主题退订和渠道降级，并让整条链路可观测地给出各渠道到达率，因为「已发送」「已投递」「已打开」是三个不同的数字。

title: Designing an Idempotent Payment Flow
contentMd:
Money has a nasty property: retrying a request must never charge twice, yet a network timeout means you cannot know whether the first attempt succeeded. That tension is what an idempotent payment flow resolves, and it earns its place as a favorite interview question.

The mechanism is an idempotency key. The client generates a unique key per logical payment intent, usually a UUID, and sends it on every retry. The server stores the key with its outcome in a dedicated table carrying a unique constraint. The first request to commit writes the result; any retry sees the existing row and returns the stored response instead of creating a second charge.

The detail interviewers probe is the concurrent case. Two identical requests can arrive simultaneously, so the unique index is your safety net: one insert wins, the other raises a conflict and then re-reads. Never check-then-act without that constraint. The record must also be written in the same transaction as the state transition, or a crash between them leaves dangerous ambiguity.

Then handle the longer semantics. Keys expire after some hours so storage does not grow forever. Payments have real states too: created, authorized, captured, refunded. Scope the key to the intent, use separate keys for capture and refund, reconcile against provider webhooks, treat the provider's own idempotency header as defense in depth, and confirm the client reuses the same key rather than minting a new one on retry.
contentCn:
钱有个讨厌的特性：重试请求绝不能导致重复扣款，但网络超时又让你无法知道第一次尝试是否成功。这种张力正是幂等支付流程要解决的，它成为高频面试题绝非偶然。

核心机制是幂等键。客户端为每次逻辑支付意图生成一个唯一键（通常是 UUID），并在每次重试时都带上它。服务端把这个键及其结果写入一张带唯一约束的专用表。第一个提交成功的请求写入结果；后续任何重试看到已有行，就直接返回存储好的响应，而不会产生第二笔扣款。

面试官会追问的实现细节是并发场景。两个相同请求可能同时到达，所以唯一索引就是你的安全网：一次插入成功，另一次抛出冲突异常后再回查。绝不能在没有该约束的情况下「先查后写」。这条记录还必须与状态变更写在同一个事务里，否则中途崩溃会留下危险的歧义。

然后再处理更长的语义。键应该在若干小时后过期，避免存储无限膨胀。支付本身也有真实的状态机：已创建、已授权、已捕获、已退款。要把幂等键的作用域限定在意图上，捕获和退款各自使用不同的键，要与支付服务商的 webhook 对账，把服务商自带的幂等头当作纵深防御，并确认客户端重试时复用同一个键，而不是重新生成一个。

title: Distributed Unique ID Generation
contentMd:
Auto-increment primary keys do not survive horizontal scaling: two shards will happily both issue ID 42. So every distributed system eventually needs a way to mint unique IDs across nodes, ideally without any coordination in the hot path.

UUIDv4 is the zero-effort answer: 128 random bits, generated locally, no collisions in practice. Its flaws are real though. It is not sortable by time, it is 36 characters as text, and fully random values wreck B-tree locality because every insert lands somewhere different.

Snowflake is the standard upgrade. Pack the ID into 64 bits: a millisecond timestamp, a machine or datacenter ID, and a per-node sequence number. IDs are unique because no two nodes share a machine ID, roughly time-ordered because the timestamp leads, and sortable so indexes stay sequential. The operational cost is clock management: you must assign node IDs, handle skew, and decide what happens on clock rollback.

Alternatives worth mentioning include database-backed ticket servers that lease blocks of IDs, which are simple and monotonic but add a dependency and a hotspot, and ULID or UUIDv7, newer standards that keep a time prefix for sortability. Be clear about which properties you actually need: uniqueness, ordering, compactness, opacity. Leaking a guessable sequence becomes a security problem the moment IDs appear in URLs.
contentCn:
自增主键无法在水平扩展中存活：两个分片会愉快地同时发出 ID 42。因此每个分布式系统最终都需要一种跨节点生成唯一 ID 的方案，而且最好在热路径上不需要任何协调动作。

UUIDv4 是最省事的答案：128 位随机数，本地生成，实践中不会碰撞。但它的缺陷是真实存在的。它无法按时间排序，作为文本有 36 个字符，而且完全随机的值会破坏 B 树的局部性，因为每次插入都落在不同的位置。

Snowflake 是标准的升级方案。把 ID 打包进 64 位：毫秒级时间戳、机器或数据中心 ID，以及每个节点内的序列号。由于没有两个节点共享同一个机器 ID，所以 ID 唯一；由于时间戳在前，所以大致按时间有序，索引因此可以保持顺序写入。运维上的代价是时钟管理：你必须分配节点 ID、处理时钟偏移，并决定时钟回拨时怎么办。

值得一提的替代方案还有：基于数据库的发号服务器批量租出 ID 段，简单且单调，但引入了依赖和一个热点；以及 ULID 或 UUIDv7 这类较新的标准，它们保留了时间前缀因而可排序。要清楚说出你真正需要哪些性质：唯一性、有序性、紧凑性、不可猜测性。一旦 ID 出现在 URL 里，泄漏一个可预测的序列就成了安全问题。
titleCn: 分布式唯一 ID 生成

title: Designing Search Autocomplete
contentMd:
Autocomplete is a latency product. Users type roughly every 200 milliseconds, so anything slower than 100 milliseconds feels broken, and requests arrive in bursts that make caching unusually effective.

The classic structure is a trie over known queries, where each node holds the top N suggestions computed offline. Aggregating search logs gives you the frequency of every query; you sort them, keep perhaps the top five per prefix, then materialize the trie periodically. Because the tree can reach hundreds of gigabytes, shard it by prefix so the first character routes you to the right server, and keep everything in memory.

That offline-only design means trending topics never appear, which interviewers love to poke at. The fix is a hybrid: serve from the static trie for instant results, then asynchronously update a small layer of recent trends so a breaking news query starts appearing within a minute. Ranking should blend raw popularity with personalization and a freshness boost.

Client-side details matter too. Debounce requests, cancel in-flight fetches when a newer keystroke arrives, and cache responses per prefix locally. Do not forget offensive content filtering, per-language tries, and the cold-start problem where a brand-new deployment has no search history to learn from.
contentCn:
自动补全是一个延迟敏感型产品。用户大约每 200 毫秒敲一个键，所以任何超过 100 毫秒的响应都会让人觉得卡；同时请求是成突发到来的，这让缓存格外有效。

经典结构是建立在已知查询词上的 Trie 树，每个节点保存离线算好的前 N 条建议。聚合搜索日志可以得到每个查询的出现频次，把它们排序后为每个前缀保留大约五条，再定期把 Trie 物化出来。由于这棵树可能高达数百 GB，要按前缀把它分片，让首字符就能路由到正确的服务器，并全部放在内存里。

纯离线的设计意味着新热点永远不会出现，这正是面试官喜欢戳的点。修法是混合方案：先从静态 Trie 即时返回结果，同时异步更新一小层近期热词，这样突发新闻在一分钟内就能被补全出来。排序应当把原始热度与个性化以及新鲜度加权混合在一起。

客户端细节同样重要。要对请求去抖，当更新的按键到来时取消在途请求，并按前缀在本地缓存响应。别忘了还要做违规内容过滤、按语言拆分 Trie，以及冷启动问题——全新部署时没有任何搜索历史可供学习。

title: Leaderboard Design at Scale
contentMd:
A leaderboard looks trivial until someone asks for their rank. A relational ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 10 is fine for thousands of users and a disaster past a million, because sorting on every request costs O(N log N).

The canonical answer is Redis sorted sets. Each entry is a member with a numeric score inside a ZSET: ZADD updates a score in logarithmic time, ZREVRANGE returns any page of the ranking instantly, and ZREVRANK gives a user's exact position. Ties are usually broken by folding a timestamp into the fractional part of the score, since sorted sets break equal scores lexicographically by member.

Scale past one Redis instance by bucketing the ZSET by score range, such as bronze, silver, and gold, so each shard holds a slice of players and you only consult the buckets relevant to a requested page. Keeping SQL as the durable source of truth and rebuilding or updating Redis asynchronously is a common, defensible split.

Finally decide the time semantics. All-time, weekly, and daily boards are three different keys, and rolling windows need either periodic resets or per-period keys with a TTL. For users buried deep in the list, do not compute an exact rank; return a percentile bucket and say so, because nobody cares whether they rank 41,283rd or 41,290th.
contentCn:
排行榜看起来很简单，直到有人问「我排第几」。在关系库里直接 ORDER BY score DESC LIMIT 10，几千个用户没问题，超过一百万就是灾难，因为每次请求都要承担 O(N log N) 的排序开销。

标准答案是 Redis 有序集合。每个条目是 ZSET 中的一个成员加上一个数值 score：ZADD 以对数时间更新分数，ZREVRANGE 瞬间返回任意一页榜单，ZREVRANK 给出某个用户的精确名次。分数相同时通常把时间戳折叠进 score 的小数部分，因为有序集合对同分成员是按字典序排列的。

要扩展到单个 Redis 实例之上，可以按分数区间把 ZSET 分桶，例如青铜、白银、黄金，这样每个分片只持有一部分玩家，取某一页时只需查询与请求相关的桶。用关系型数据库作为持久化的真相来源，再异步地重建或更新 Redis，也是一种常见且站得住脚的分工。

最后要确定时间语义。总榜、周榜、日榜是三个不同的 key；滚动窗口要么定期重置，要么使用带 TTL 的按周期 key。对于排在很后面的用户，不要去计算精确名次——返回一个百分位区间并明确告知即可，因为没人在意自己是第 41,283 名还是第 41,290 名。

title: Multi-Region Deployment Tradeoffs
contentMd:
Multi-region deployment exists for two reasons: latency, because users in Sydney should not wait on a datacenter in Virginia, and availability, because a regional outage should not take down the whole product. Everything hard about it comes from the speed of light and from CAP.

Start with routing. Latency-based or geo DNS sends users to their nearest healthy region, and anycast gives you failover at the BGP level. Stateless request handling duplicates easily everywhere; the data layer is where every design gets difficult.

For reads you can replicate to every region and accept staleness. For writes you must choose. Single-region writes keep correctness simple but impose cross-region latency on half your users. Multi-region writes risk conflicts that last-writer-wins resolves badly, unless you use CRDTs, per-user write routing where a home region owns each user's data, or a globally consistent store that trades latency for correctness. Most real systems admit they are read-local, write-global, and carefully bound the parts that cannot be.

Do not forget failure drills. Practice actual regional evacuation on a schedule, keep N+1 capacity per region so one failure does not cascade, replicate your deployment artifacts and secrets too, and stay honest about data residency laws, which sometimes forbid replication no matter what the architecture prefers.
contentCn:
多区域部署存在两个理由：一是延迟，悉尼的用户不该等着弗吉尼亚的数据中心响应；二是可用性，某个区域故障不应该拖垮整个产品。它所有困难的地方都来自光速和 CAP。

先从路由讲起。基于延迟或地理位置的 DNS 把用户送到最近的健康区域，任播（anycast）则提供 BGP 级别的故障转移。无状态的请求处理层很容易在各处复制；数据层才是每个设计都变得艰难的地方。

对于读，你可以复制到每个区域并接受陈旧。对于写，你必须做出选择。单区域写入让正确性变得简单，却让一半用户承担跨区延迟。多区域写入则冒着冲突风险，而「最后写入者获胜」的解法往往很糟——除非你使用 CRDT、按用户路由写入（由用户的归属区域拥有其数据），或者使用一个用延迟换取正确性的全局一致存储。大多数真实系统会坦诚承认自己是「本地读、全局写」，并小心地划出那些做不到的边界。

别忘了故障演练。要按计划真实练习区域疏散，每个区域都留出 N+1 容量以免单点故障引发雪崩，部署产物和密钥也要一并复制，并且坦诚对待数据驻留法律——有时候法律会禁止复制，无论架构多想这么做。

title: Capacity Estimation Basics for Interviews
contentMd:
Interviewers ask for back-of-envelope numbers not because the arithmetic is hard but because it reveals whether you know which levers exist. Always begin by restating assumptions out loud: monthly active users, the daily active fraction, requests per user per day, and the read-to-write ratio.

Convert everything into a rate. Ten million daily actives making twenty requests each means 200 million requests per day, which is roughly 2,300 per second on average, and you must multiply by a peak factor of two to five because traffic is never flat. Storage follows the same shape: estimate bytes per record, multiply by new records per second, then multiply by time. Ten million new one-kilobyte rows daily is about 3.6 TB per year, before replicas and indexes.

Then translate rates into machines. A well-tuned server might handle a thousand simple reads per second, so 5,000 peak reads per second needs five or six nodes plus headroom. Memory math matters just as much: if 20 percent of your data serves 80 percent of requests, size the cache for that working set, not for the entire dataset.

Close the loop by sanity-checking your own answers. Does the storage figure fit on one machine? Is the bandwidth plausible? Saying out loud that the whole working set fits comfortably inside a single Redis instance, therefore caching is cheap here, is exactly the kind of insight the question is hunting for.
contentCn:
面试官要求做粗略估算，不是因为算术难，而是因为这能暴露你是否知道有哪些可调的杠杆。永远先从大声复述假设开始：月活用户数、日活占比、每用户每日请求数，以及读写比。

把所有东西换算成速率。一千万日活每人发二十次请求，就是每天两亿次请求，平均约每秒 2,300 次；而你必须再乘上两到五倍的峰值系数，因为流量从来不是平坦的。存储照同样的思路推算：估算每条记录的字节数，乘以每秒新增记录数，再乘以时间。每天一千万条 1 KB 的新记录，大约是每年 3.6 TB，这还没算副本和索引。

然后把速率换算成机器。一台调优良好的服务器大概能扛每秒一千次简单读取，所以每秒 5,000 次峰值读取需要五到六个节点再加余量。内存计算同样重要：如果 20% 的数据服务了 80% 的请求，那就按这个工作集来规划缓存容量，而不是按全量数据。

最后要用复核自己的答案来收尾。存储量能不能放进一台机器？带宽数字是否合理？大声说出「整个工作集放进单个 Redis 实例都绰绰有余，因此这里缓存很便宜」——正是这类洞察，才是这道题真正想挖出来的东西。
